# Evidence Dossier for Daily Digest (Issue 104 | 2026-11-26)

### Section 1: Feminist Structure Signal

* **Title**:
  * **Chinese**: 伦敦 Graces Mews 画廊举办《What Rose from the Cut》：以撕裂与拼贴重构女性主义摄影史与男权档案 / 
  * **English**: Graces Mews Gallery Presents 'What Rose from the Cut': Re-examining Feminist Photo Collage and Patriarchal Archives
* **Source URL**: `https://www.theguardian.com/artanddesign/2026/nov/26/feminist-collage-artists-scissors-patriarchy`
* **Image URL**: `https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/b14f068103a23526e6a1cdf3fd151a6df58b794e/0_0_6000_4286/master/6000.jpg?width=465&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none`
* **Publication / Event Date**: November 26, 2026 (Reported by *The Guardian*; Exhibition running October 14, 2026 – January 30, 2027).
* **Verified Facts**:
  * Co-curated by artist Justine Kurland, V&A Parasol Foundation Curator of Women in Photography Fiona Rogers, and collector Sarah Miller Meigs at Graces Mews Gallery in south London.
  * Features over 40 artists across three generations working in photo collage, photomontage, and assemblage, including Martha Rosler, Claude Cahun, Frida Orupabo, Stephanie Syjuco, Linder, and Justine Kurland.
  * The show unites two core research projects: Fiona Rogers' book *Cut Out: A Feminist History of Photo Collage, Montage and Assemblage* (Thames & Hudson / V&A, 2026) and Kurland & Miller Meigs' exhibition/publication *The Rose* (2025).
  * Highlights Kurland's project *SCUMB* (*Society for Cutting Up Men's Books*), inspired by Valerie Solanas, in which canonical photography photobooks by male photographers (e.g., Lee Friedlander) are cut up to create feminist collages.
* **Relevance to Muki**: Directly addresses Muki’s core research into feminist visual culture, photobook interventions, image history, and physical tactics for dismantling patriarchal archival power through photographic collage and material destruction/reconstruction.
* **Duplication Assessment**: New signal. No overlap with recent 7 issues.

### Section 2: Visual Culture Signal

* **Title**:
  * **Chinese**: 第 12 届印度摄影节在海得拉巴开幕：呈现 30 多场展览与国际摄影书成果 / 
  * **English**: 12th Indian Photo Festival Opens in Hyderabad: Featuring Over 30 Exhibitions and Global Photobook Showcase
* **Source URL**: `https://www.thehindu.com/entertainment/art/indian-photo-festival-2026-returns-to-hyderabad-heres-what-to-expect/article71738337.ece`
* **Image URL**: `https://th-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/anoguv/article71738337.ece/alternates/FREE_1200/08_Shanti__Hyderabad.jpg`
* **Publication / Event Date**: November 26, 2026.
* **Verified Facts**:
  * Organised by Light Craft Foundation, the 12th Indian Photo Festival (IPF) opened on November 26, 2026 at the State Gallery of Art, Hyderabad, running through January 3, 2027.
  * Positioned as India's longest-running photography festival, featuring over 30 exhibitions curated from direct invitations and an international open call that received nearly 1,050 entries.
  * The program integrates artist talks, panel discussions, portfolio reviews, and dedicated photobook presentations.
  * Directed by Aquin Mathews, with an anonymous jury selection process including National Geographic photographers.
* **Relevance to Muki**: Provides insight into non-Western documentary photography, global photobook platforms, and festival infrastructure operating across South Asia and international visual networks.
* **Duplication Assessment**: New signal. No overlap with recent 7 issues.

### Section 3: China / East Asia Signal

* **Title**:
  * **Chinese**: 国立台湾美术馆开幕第十届亚洲艺术双年展：以“Mrahul Tminun·共织”重构东亚的关护与关系场域 / 
  * **English**: 10th Asian Art Biennial Opens at NTMoFA: 'Mrahul Tminun・Co-Weaving' Reframes Asia Through Indigenous and Feminist Methodologies
* **Source URL**: `https://www.e-flux.com/announcements/637380/asian-art-biennial-2026-mrahul-tminungong-zhico-weaving/`
* **Image URL**: `null` (No direct image URL meeting strict stability criteria).
* **Publication / Event Date**: Opened November 7, 2026 (Running through February 28, 2027).
* **Verified Facts**:
  * Organized by the National Taiwan Museum of Fine Arts (NTMoFA) in Taichung, curated by Lu Pei-yi (呂佩怡).
  * Brings together 30 artists and collectives, including Gudskul, Aluaiy Kaumakan (武玉玲), Labay Eyong (林介文), Citra Sasmita, Gegerboyo, and OH Haji.
  * The theme draws on the Truku Indigenous phrase *Mrahul Tminun*, which evokes the daily practice of community women gathering to weave and talk, framing "curating as weaving".
  * Focuses on Indigenous epistemologies, women's labor, queer perspectives, and collective mutual aid to approach Asia not merely as a geopolitical region but as a relational field shaped by colonial palimpsests.
* **Relevance to Muki**: Directly links East Asian visual culture with Indigenous women's craft labor, curatorial methodology ("curating as weaving"), and care-centered relational structures.
* **Duplication Assessment**: New signal. No overlap with recent 7 issues.

### Section 4: AI Research / Creative Tech Signal

* **Title**:
  * **Chinese**: 研究团队提出 Windchime 视听系统：以音频-语言模型与实时代码构建交互式多模态检索 / 
  * **English**: Researchers Introduce Windchime: Audio-Language Models and Live Coding for Interactive Audiovisual Performance Workflows
* **Source URL**: `https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26759`
* **Image URL**: `null`
* **Publication / Event Date**: November 19, 2026 (Indexed / updated Nov 23–24, 2026; Accepted to NeurIPS 2026 Creative AI Track).
* **Verified Facts**:
  * Authored by Trent Eriksen (Independent Researcher) and Celeste Betancur Gutierrez (Stanford University CCRMA).
  * Windchime is an audiovisual installation framework that processes spoken user prompts using local Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and an Audio-Language Model (ALM).
  * Rather than generating unconstrained media, the system performs embedding retrieval over a 406-stem artist-authored corpus, outputting soundscapes layered with live-coded Strudel fragments.
  * Simultaneously retrieves interactive Three.js animation scenes controlled physically via monome grid and arc hardware, distributing agency between the author, the retrieval model, and the audience.
* **Relevance to Muki**: Materially demonstrates how multimodal AI agents and audio-language models can operate within physical hardware workflows and live-coding environments as structured retrieval agents over human-authored archives, avoiding speculative generation anxiety.
* **Duplication Assessment**: New signal. No overlap with recent 7 issues.

### Section 5: Archive / Long Read / Opportunity

* **Title**:
  * **Chinese**: 芝加哥 ARC 画廊与 ATHENA 基金会启动 2027 驻留招募：提供 10 个月远程研究、1500 美元资助与个展机会 / 
  * **English**: ARC Gallery and ATHENA Fund Launch Call for 2027 Remote Artist Residency and Exhibition Program
* **Source URL**: `https://chicagogallerynews.com/news/2026/11/chicagos-arc-gallery-launches-its-first-artist-residency`
* **Image URL**: `null`
* **Publication / Event Date**: November 26, 2026.
* **Verified Facts**:
  * Organized by ARC Gallery & Educational Foundation (a women-run artist cooperative founded in Chicago in 1973 during the feminist movement) and supported by philanthropic partner ATHENA.
  * The ARC + ATHENA Artist Residency is a 10-month remote program (February to November 2027) open to three emerging international artists working in any medium.
  * Selected artists receive a $1,500 stipend ($1,200 artist stipend + $300 shipping allowance), remote curatorial mentorship/peer dialogue, and three concurrent solo exhibitions at ARC Gallery in November 2027.
  * Application deadline: December 15, 2026.
* **Relevance to Muki**: High-quality opportunity directly connected to feminist institution-building, artist-run infrastructure, remote research workflows, and career support for emerging visual practice.
* **Duplication Assessment**: New signal. No overlap with recent 7 issues.
